correctness.rationale: For any smooth real coordinate-tangent quadric, B=A^-1 is invertible symmetric with trace zero and zero diagonal. Its determinant has the explicit quartic expansion. Inertia is (2,2) iff det B>0; the other cases have Witt index one and no real projective line. A real line-product would contain a real line, proving necessity. In the split case the real Segre model and real rank-one factorization of the four tangent coordinate sections construct real lines whose product map is the Segre isomorphism. The two real ruling orders yield precisely two free reciprocal-torus orbits; signatures also give the real torus/sphere topology. The standalone code ran exact symbolic identities and 128 supplementary finite inertia checks; computations do not substitute for the general proof.

This new theorem answers the natural real inverse question for its five-parameter real family with an exact quartic sign test, including the real factorization orbit count, total pointwise surjectivity, and topology change from torus to sphere. The negative-sign region provides a real-point-bearing quadric with complex but no real pair of line factors. This is a complete structural boundary of a natural parameter family, not an arbitrary numerical slice or a claim to new real quadratic-form theory.
